page: Amazon Web Services r6in.metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server powered by Intel Xeon 8375C processors built on the x86_64 architecture. The platform exposes 64 physical cores and 128 dedicated execution threads operating at clock speeds up to 3.5 GHz, supported by 54 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates instruction set extensions including AVX-512 with VNNI, AES, and Total Memory Encryption. System memory provides 1024 GB of DDR4 running at 3 GHz, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Network connectivity is provisioned at a 200 Gbps baseline. The system contains no integrated local storage and no GPUs, requiring network-attached storage architectures for persistent data.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core computational density alongside high memory throughput. The server scores within the top tiers for PassMark CPU computation, encryption algorithms, and ray tracing benchmarks, paired with 125022.52 on multi-core stress-ng tests. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 338.95 GB/sec, supporting high-throughput memory operations such as 111.35 million Redis SET operations per second. In contrast, single-thread performance benchmarks register within mid-tier averages, and the omission of local NVMe storage concentrates storage I/O throughput on external storage attachments.

From an infrastructure perspective, r6in.metal provides direct bare-metal access without virtualization overhead, pairing extensive RAM density with high-bandwidth network throughput. This configuration targets resource profiles requiring massive memory spaces and consistent inter-node communication, including distributed in-memory databases, enterprise caching layers, and high-throughput data transformation pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r6in.metal is a bare-metal memory-optimized instance featuring 64 physical cores and 128 dedicated vCPUs on Intel Xeon 8375C processors alongside 1024 GB of DDR4 system memory. Operating on the x86_64 architecture at clock speeds up to 3.5 GHz, the server includes AVX-512 vector extensions, cryptographic acceleration, and an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU distribution. Networking is provisioned with a 200 Gbps baseline interface. Benchmark results show top-tier multi-threaded PassMark CPU performance, ray tracing capacity, and strong memory bandwidth reaching 338.95 GB/sec for uncached reads, driving over 111 million Redis SET operations per second. Tradeoffs include average single-threaded benchmark results and the absence of integrated local storage or GPUs. The bare-metal platform is structured for large in-memory databases, distributed caches, and memory-bound ETL workflows.
